_meta.status: DECLARED — implementation lands in Phase C1 of the 2.0 federation work package.
_meta.stability: Frozen for the weft-generation lifetime per ADR-002. Shape additions that preserve wire compatibility (new optional response fields) are allowed; breaking changes require a new generation.
_meta.relation_to_classic: Same request shape (bytes-identical). Response shape differs: weft wraps ScanIngestResult in a BatchResponse-style envelope — new_finding_ids becomes succeeded (BatchResponse.succeeded), per-finding ingest failures become failed (a list of {index, fingerprint, code, reason} entries addressed by request position; empty when nothing was dropped), replayed findings are listed under unchanged, counts move to a stats sibling (now including requested/applied), warnings stay at the top level as operator text.

request_optional_fields.scanned_paths: list[str]  # OPTIONAL. The authoritative set of files the scanner visited this run, including clean files with zero findings. Wire-compatible addition (omitting it preserves prior behaviour). When mark_unseen is true, the absent-fingerprint sweep is driven off {files-with-findings} ∪ {scanned_paths}, so a file whose last/only finding was fixed (and is therefore absent from findings) is still reconciled to unseen_in_latest and its linked issue cascade-closes. With scanned_paths non-empty, mark_unseen=true + findings=[] is a valid fully-clean scan (no longer a 400). Unknown clean paths (no prior file record) are skipped, never created.

response_shape.succeeded: list[str]  # server-generated finding ids for newly-created findings (was: new_finding_ids in classic)
response_shape.failed: list[ScanFindingFailureWeft]  # per-finding ingest failures, always present ([] when nothing was dropped). Each entry: {index: int (position in the request findings array), fingerprint: str|null, code: str, reason: str}. The code vocabulary is OPEN - treat an unknown code as a generic rejection. Documented codes: OVER_CAP (finding dropped by the registry's per-path body cap; emitted today), VALIDATION (malformed finding; reserved - a malformed finding currently rejects the whole batch with HTTP 400), SCHEME_MISMATCH (fingerprint scheme differs from the store's; reserved - carried batch-level by weft_reasons today, the findings are still ingested), KIND_NOT_ACCEPTED (Stage 0 telemetry cut; emitted today: the finding's kind - metadata.wardline.kind when it is a known non-defect kind (fact/classification/metric/suggestion), otherwise defect (a missing, malformed, or unknown kind counts as defect) - is not in the project's scan_ingest.accept_kinds (default ["defect"]; ["*"] accepts everything), or its path is the <engine> pseudo-path while "*" is not accepted. reason is 'telemetry kinds are not work; see Stage 0'). The effective accept_kinds is advertised as accept_kinds on GET /api/files/_schema (and /api/weft/files/_schema). Additive: a consumer that ignores failed still sees the same succeeded/stats/warnings.
response_shape.unchanged: list[{id: str, reason: 'already_present'}]  # always present ([] when none). Findings the batch matched to an already-stored row with identical content (same scan_source + fingerprint) - a replayed batch. They are NOT in succeeded (succeeded stays newly-created ids); a finding that matched but whose content changed is counted in stats.findings_updated, not listed here.

stats.requested: int  # number of findings in the request
stats.applied: int  # findings_created + findings_updated; requested - applied is what failed[] itemises (plus the unchanged replays, which count as updated)
stats.rejected_by_kind: int  # findings rejected with KIND_NOT_ACCEPTED (Stage 0): a metadata.wardline.kind outside the project's scan_ingest.accept_kinds, or an <engine> pseudo-path row. Each is also itemised in failed[].

response_shape.warnings: list[str]  # operator text only (e.g. unknown severity coerced to 'info'; the human-readable twin of a failed[] entry). Machine-readable outcomes live in failed / unchanged.

shape_decl.external_adapter_contract: Filigree does not parse SARIF on this endpoint. External SARIF adapters MUST map SARIF result.partialFingerprints or result.fingerprints into each scan-results finding.fingerprint before POSTing. Filigree then preserves finding.fingerprint through ingest, readback, promotion, fingerprint dedup, stale/fixed transitions, and reopen-on-regress lifecycle handling. Fingerprint-less legacy findings remain accepted and use the file/source/rule/line heuristic.
shape_decl.rationale: BatchResponse-style wrapper per ADR-002 §1 and work-package Phase A2. Scan-results has mixed semantics (batch ingest + summary counts); the envelope honours the batch-semantics-where-applicable rule by exposing succeeded/failed (per-finding granularity) while preserving the counts signal in a stats sibling. Named subtype so future weft endpoints with similar mixed semantics have a pattern to follow.

examples.name: success_clean_file_via_scanned_paths
examples.note: Close-on-fixed driver. An agent fixed the only finding in src/a.py; the re-scan carries no findings for it but lists it in scanned_paths with mark_unseen=true. Filigree flips the now-absent finding to unseen_in_latest and cascade-closes its linked issue. Cascade outcomes are logged, not surfaced in the envelope.

examples.name: partial_kind_not_accepted_reports_failed
examples.note: Stage 0 telemetry cut under the default scan_ingest.accept_kinds (["defect"]). Finding 0 is a defect and is ingested. Finding 1 carries a telemetry kind (metadata.wardline.kind = fact) and finding 2 sits on the <engine> pseudo-path; both are rejected per-finding with KIND_NOT_ACCEPTED (index is the position in the REQUEST array), counted in stats.rejected_by_kind, and never written.
